subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should first-time arbitrary plugin installs fail closed unless they resolve through ClawHub or OpenClaw-owned bundled/catalog metadata, while tracked updates and selected guided flows remain exempt?
rationale: The implementation and proof establish coherent behavior, but deciding which executable sources bypass warnings and whether existing unattended commands may break is a security and compatibility policy choice requiring maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve current trust model
options.body: Keep the centralized classification, interactive warning, separate noninteractive acknowledgement, chat restrictions, and documented trusted-flow exemptions.

options.title: Preserve unattended compatibility
options.body: Retain current noninteractive behavior and expose strict provenance acknowledgement as an opt-in policy.

options.title: Split the policy
options.body: Separate plugin-install provenance gating from the broader Crestodian approval changes for independent owner review.

recommendation.title: Approve current trust model
recommendation.body: Keep the centralized classification, interactive warning, separate noninteractive acknowledgement, chat restrictions, and documented trusted-flow exemptions.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history shows the strongest ownership of central plugin-install safety, persistence, and related policy paths.
